title: Introduction to Networks (CCNA 1)
subtitle: Build, address and secure a small network with Cisco devices
audience_line: Students, technicians and IT staff starting the CCNA path
overview: This programme is the first of three courses that prepare the Cisco CCNA 200-301 exam, aligned with Cisco Networking Academy Introduction to Networks v7. Participants learn how networks are built and how data moves through them, configure Cisco switches and routers, design IPv4 addressing plans with subnetting and VLSM, deploy IPv6, and secure devices with strong passwords and SSH. Every chapter ends with a lab in Cisco Packet Tracer, and the programme closes with a final project in which each participant designs, builds and documents a small business network. Switching, Routing & Wireless Essentials (CCNA 2) follows.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Students, technicians and IT staff starting the CCNA path

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: None. Basic computer use; comfort with binary numbers helps and is reviewed in the course

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 39 h: 33 h of chapters + 6 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs on simulated Cisco devices

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs locally: one laptop per participant with Cisco Packet Tracer (free with each participant’s Cisco Networking Academy account); physical Cisco switches and routers for selected labs when the organiser provides a rack; no cloud account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can build a small switched and routed network, plan IPv4 and IPv6 addressing with subnetting and VLSM, secure Cisco devices and troubleshoot basic connectivity

phases.name: Network Fundamentals
phases.focus: Network types, reference models, first device configuration
phases.intro: Participants learn what a network is made of and how the OSI and TCP/IP models describe it, then take their first steps in Cisco IOS on switches and end devices. Validated lab: a switch with a hostname, passwords, a management address and a saved configuration, reachable from a PC.

chapters.title: Networks & Models
chapters.content: Components, topologies, network types, OSI and TCP/IP models, standards

chapters.title: Basic Device Configuration
chapters.content: Cisco IOS, switch and end-device configuration

phases.name: From Links to Packets
phases.focus: Media, Ethernet and switching, IP packets, ARP and Neighbor Discovery
phases.intro: Participants follow data from the cable to the packet: media and Ethernet frames, how a switch learns MAC addresses, then how IPv4 and IPv6 packets are routed and how addresses are resolved. Validated lab: a captured exchange that shows a MAC table filling, an ARP request and an IPv6 neighbor solicitation, on hosts addressed in advance by the trainer, observed in Packet Tracer simulation mode.

chapters.title: Physical & Data Link Layers
chapters.content: Media, Ethernet frames, MAC addresses, switching, MAC address tables

chapters.title: Network Layer & Address Resolution
chapters.content: IPv4 and IPv6 packets, routing, ARP and IPv6 Neighbor Discovery

phases.name: Routers & IP Addressing
phases.focus: Router configuration, IPv4, subnetting and VLSM, IPv6
phases.intro: Participants configure a router as the default gateway, then learn IP addressing in depth: IPv4 structure and binary, subnetting and VLSM design, IPv6 address types, SLAAC and IPv6 subnetting. Validated lab: a VLSM addressing plan for a site with several LANs behind one router, implemented in dual stack and verified with ping and traceroute.

chapters.title: IPv4 Addressing
chapters.content: Address structure, binary, unicast, broadcast and multicast, public and private addresses

phases.name: Transport, Services & Security
phases.focus: ICMP, TCP and UDP, DNS, DHCP, HTTP, securing a small network
phases.intro: Participants see how applications use the network through ICMP, TCP, UDP, DNS, DHCP and HTTP, then secure the devices of a small network against common threats with strong passwords and SSH. Validated lab: a small network where hosts get addresses from DHCP and reach a web server by name, and every device is managed only over SSH.

chapters.title: Transport & Application Layers
chapters.content: ICMP, TCP and UDP, DNS, DHCP, HTTP

chapters.title: Security Basics & Small Networks
chapters.content: Threats, passwords, SSH, securing devices, building a small network

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A small business network, documented and presented
phases.intro: Each participant designs and builds the network of a small business from a written brief, reusing the phase labs, then documents it and troubleshoots faults injected by the trainer.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, write the VLSM addressing plan, build the topology in dual stack IPv4 and IPv6

chapters.title: Harden & Document
chapters.content: Device hardening and SSH access, addressing table, topology diagram, saved configurations

chapters.title: Troubleshoot & Review
chapters.content: Find and fix faults injected by the trainer; questions and feedback

project.title: Small Business Network
project.brief: The network of a small business with a VLSM addressing plan, IPv4 and IPv6 connectivity, hardened Cisco devices managed over SSH, and documentation that lets another technician troubleshoot it.
project.stack: Cisco Packet Tracer, Cisco IOS switches and routers, IPv4, IPv6, SSH
project.deliverable: Packet Tracer file, addressing table, topology diagram, device configurations
